executiveSummary: GM0597 passes the complete deterministic model contract for all ten canonical presets, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Its 2025 CBS/PDOK identity, 47,999 residents, twelve neighbourhoods/districts, one BAG place, nine BRT settlements, 80 scheduled-transit stop areas and six A15/A16/A38/N915 municipal-border routes are coherent. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Ridderkerk is a low-lying IJsselmonde municipality beside the tidal Nieuwe Maas and Noord, protected by primary and historic dikes but also containing riverfront land outside primary-defence protection. Municipal evidence distinguishes primary-defence, outside-dike, polder/surface-water, sewer, groundwater, subsidence and pluvial pathways and records severe 29 May 2018 rainfall impacts. The model selects none of those mechanisms, yet reports an exact generic 2.824966 m river depth from T+12 through T+72, 24,653 affected people-equivalent and 1,796,117.29 person-hours by T+72; its separate coastal preset reports zero direct inundation despite official benedenrivieren evidence that sea level, tide, wind, storm-surge barriers and river discharge interact. Seven unrelated active hazard families reuse one exact twelve-neighbourhood order. The graph omits polder/sewer/pump/groundwater causality, outside-dike access, A15/A16 crossing and junction common modes, industrial or dangerous-goods releases, dynamic riverfront/business populations, external acute care and governed drinking-water, electricity, gas and telecom topology. Scheduled September/October 2026 road works and grid-congestion/project records are lifecycle/planning evidence, not the live operating state on the 3 September audit reference. Retain real hazard eligibility, non-residential demand, bounded remote-hazard screens and Mobility/Supply-only road scope. Suppress unsupported physical depth, local rank, affected, service and recovery precision. NoData, no selected case, a plan, a scheduled restriction, a register object or an observation never means zero, safe, open, operational or recovered.

evidenceSources.title: E01 — Wijken en buurten 2025, full administrative geometry, BAG place and BRT settlements
evidenceSources.edition: 2025 administrative/statistical editions; generated sources retrieved 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-02
supports: Fresh CBS OData for GM0597 reports Ridderkerk, 47,999 residents, density 2,045/km², 11,750 residents age 65+ and 7,547 one-person households: https://opendata.cbs.nl/ODataApi/OData/86165NED/TypedDataSet?%24filter=WijkenEnBuurten%20eq%20%27GM0597%20%20%20%20%27&%24select=WijkenEnBuurten%2CGemeentenaam_1%2CAantalInwoners_5%2CBevolkingsdichtheid_34%2Ck_65JaarOfOuder_12%2CEenpersoonshuishoudens_30. CBS cells are independently rounded or suppressed and nulls are not zeros.

The current non-generalized GM0597 MultiPolygon has 1,261 coordinate positions, versus 59 positions in the generated overview geometry; the generated center [4.598346242020436, 51.86636867675748] lies inside both.

The consumed regional data contain twelve official neighbourhoods/districts, one active BAG place named Ridderkerk and nine BRT settlements: Bolnes, Oostendam, Oude Molen, Ridderkerk, Rijsoord, Roergebied, Slikkerveer, Zwaantje and Zwet.

CBS/administrative geography is reference context, not a dike compartment, hydraulic domain, sewer catchment, evacuation zone or utility topology. Edition, retrieval time, generalized/full-resolution role, coverage and missing-value semantics must remain visible.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Strategie Klimaatadaptatie Ridderkerk 2022–2026
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal strategy for 2022–2026; underlying stress-test and historic-event context as stated in the document
supports: The strategy says parts of IJsselmonde lie up to about two metres below NAP. It distinguishes the primary Oostmolendijk/Ringdijk defence along Noord/Nieuwe Maas, Pruimendijk/Waaldijk/Noldijk along the Waal, historic dikes/compartments and intensively used outside-dike riverfront areas that are raised to differing degrees.
It describes the coupled influence of sea level, river discharge and storm-surge barriers and therefore supports tidal/benedenrivieren eligibility, not an independent open-coast all-clear.

On 29 May 2018, roughly 50–70 mm fell in a short period and the Rijksstraatweg tunnel flooded. A 70 mm/hour stress test treated roads with at least 15 cm water as impassable and highlighted Slikkerveer, Bolnes and Centrum for expected water nuisance.

The sewer is not designed for such extreme rain; overflow can bring contaminated water onto streets or into surface water. The document also identifies high groundwater, drought-related groundwater decline and subsidence, older peat-founded buildings, salinity/water-quality pressure and heat on paved areas.

Strategy maps, historic observations and stress-test classes support mechanism eligibility and preparedness. They have no incident cadence or complete native raster/NoData/licence contract in the consumed application and do not validate current depth, passability or operational state.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Programma Stedelijk Water 2023–2027, water-system inventory and Beheerplan Water 2026–2030
evidenceSources.edition: Water-management plan 2026–2030; Programma Stedelijk Water adopted 2023-05-25; 2026 budget inventory
supports: The official 2026–2030 plan inventories about 37 km of municipally maintained watercourse, 27 km of revetment, 5.5 km of culverts, 18 weirs, eight drainage/suppletion pumps and 184 culverts. It explicitly leaves water-safety tasks outside its scope and points to water-board registers for responsibilities.

The 2026 municipal budget reports planning-scale assets including 291 km sewer, 50 km pressure sewer/force main, 23,800 connections, 48 sewer pumps, 119 pressure-sewer pumps, three tunnel pumps, three surface-water pumps, seven settling/storage facilities and two storage sewers: https://raad.ridderkerk.nl/Documenten/Programmabegroting-2026-en-Meerjarenraming-2027-2029.pdf.

The Programma Stedelijk Water 2023–2027 was formally adopted on 25 May 2023: https://zoek.officielebekendmakingen.nl/gmb-2023-266648.html. Policy periods and replacement works are lifecycle context, not proof that an asset is connected, running, alarm-free or capable under a selected event.

The inventories do not publish compatible live pump throughput, catchment connectivity, receiving-water state, power/backup, overflow/quality, telemetry alarms, crews or restoration. Those fields remain Unknown.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Primary dike trajectory 17-3 and IJsselmonde Noordoost water-system planning
evidenceSources.edition: Current project and area-plan pages retrieved 2026-09-03
supports: WSHD identifies Oostdijk, Donkerslootsedijk and Oostmolendijk as primary trajectory 17-3 in eastern Ridderkerk. The current project page says the dike is safe under present requirements while components require work toward future standards; the project has been shifted/paused. Future work is not a current breach or unsafe-state flag.
WSHD's Oostmolendijk overview likewise separates current monitoring/sufficiency from future strengthening needs: https://www.wshd.nl/oostmolendijk.

The IJsselmonde Noordoost water-area process says urbanisation reduces infiltration and future pump capacity is needed; it describes the 1964 Oud- en Nieuw-Reijerwaard pumping arrangement as insufficient for the future configuration, with decisions expected in 2027 and implementation taking years. This is planning evidence, not a present pump failure.
Dike/project and water-area pages do not select a breach/overtopping case, source hydrograph, operational level decision, connected inundation, pump state, response resource or recovery time.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel Rotterdam-Rijnmond 2026–2029, versie 1.0
supports: The official regional-context document lists extreme rainfall, failure of primary/regional barriers, electricity, telecom, cyber, hazardous-substance production/storage/transport and transport disruption among material Rotterdam-Rijnmond risks.

It distinguishes flooding after primary-defence failure from regional-water mechanisms and identifies cross-sector dependencies from electricity into drinking water, wastewater, health, mobility and telecom, including emergency drinking-water planning beyond 24 hours.

The profile is strategic scenario evidence and explicitly does not supply local response-capability detail. It does not publish Ridderkerk incident probability, source/perimeter, operator topology, live asset state, staff/resources or restoration forecasts.
Final post-consultation adoption was not independently established during this audit; the source has no live machine cadence or explicit standard document-reuse licence stated.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / PDOK, ProRail, NDW and OVapi
evidenceSources.title: E06 — NWB routes, Rotterdam road-work planning, crossings and scheduled transit
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-light 2026-08-01; ProRail/NDW current snapshots and OVapi schedule context; RWS pages current 2026-09-03
supports: The generated network contains six logical border routes: two A15 links, two A16 links, one A38 link and one N915 link. They are static municipal-border corridor abstractions, not structure-level, directional, real-time or emergency-route capacity.

At the 3 September 2026 audit reference, the RWS plan lists A15 work starting 4 September, Vaanplein closures on 11–14 September and A16 Ridderkerk–Terbregseplein work on 2–5 October. These are future scheduled restrictions, not present closure on 3 September.

RWS separately announced two future A16 Van Brienenoordbrug night closures on 9–10 September, with detours and arrangements for emergency/OV services: https://www.rijkswaterstaat.nl/nieuws/archief/2026/09/a16-van-brienenoordbrug-2-nachten-dicht-voor-onderhoud-9-10-september-2026. The bridge over the Nieuwe Maas is a critical external continuation of the Ridderkerk–Rotterdam corridor, not encoded as a graph structure.

The A15 Noordtunnel beneath the Noord and the movable N915 Bridge over the Noord are downstream cross-boundary dependencies east of the generated Ridderkerk–Hendrik-Ido-Ambacht links. The A16 also depends on Ridderster/Vaanplein junctions and more distant Oude-Maas crossing routes; the six local edges do not encode those common modes or alternatives.

There is no ProRail station inside GM0597 and the deployed timetable has 80 stop areas. Static geometry and scheduled stops do not prove train/bus/waterborne service, vehicles, accessible evacuation capacity, freight presence or incident operation.
The cached NDW/transport-restriction assignment found no authoritative local match. That scoped no-match is not proof that any road, bridge, tunnel, junction, railway or scheduled service is open.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Gebiedsvisie Rivieroevers, PlanMER and Omgevingsvisie
evidenceSources.edition: Rivieroevers vision/PlanMER adopted in 2021; current environment-vision context retrieved 2026-09-03
supports: The municipal riverfront evidence covers the Nieuwe Maas and Noord and identifies riverfront locations outside primary-defence protection as well as water-related businesses, housing, recreation, access and environmental constraints. Outside-dike does not mean uniformly unraised or uniformly inundated.

The current municipal environment-vision context identifies Donkersloot and Cornelisland as important business areas and links Bolnes/Slikkerveer development to river activity: https://lokaleregelgeving.overheid.nl/CVDR744157/1.

Business/industrial land, port/waterway activity and A15/A16 dangerous-goods context imply event-time workers, visitors, logistics users and potentially source-specific hazardous-material pathways that resident counts cannot represent.

The planning documents do not establish current hazardous inventories, a release, wind/dispersion, exposed indoor/outdoor population, facility occupancy, emergency resources, contamination or clearance. Those remain Unknown unless a competent incident or permit authority supplies a selected case.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschapshuis/WSHD, Stedin/NBNL, RDI, RIVM, DUO, KNMI, Waterinfo and NDW
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Public water, grid, telecom, facilities and observation context
evidenceSources.edition: Deployed context snapshots 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-03; individual publisher records retain their own versions and valid times
supports: The cache assigns 163 HWH objects: one sewer pump, one RWZI, 20 surface-water pumps and 141 weirs. HWH is contributor-dependent partial register coverage; lifecycle status and nominal capacities do not establish catchments, compatible throughput, live controls, power/backup or performance.

One NBNL postcode sample covers Stedin service area CM48 Langeland with planning values and an earliest project year of 2026. Stedin's congestion study reports materially insufficient available flexibility and multi-year expansion timing for the wider Langeland area. These are capacity/planning constraints, not current load, topology, outage or restoration.

Ridderkerk's 3 September 2026 net-congestion notice explains municipal development constraints and actions: https://www.ridderkerk.nl/actueel/netcongestie-wat-is-het-en-wat-betekent-het-voor-onze-gemeente/. Publication on the audit date does not make it evidence of a power interruption.

The caches contain 68 antenna registrations and 28 education sites, but no surveyed acute emergency department inside GM0597. Nearest surveyed 24/7 ED is Maasstad Ziekenhuis Rotterdam about 4.599 km straight-line away; its annual 16-room/35,150-visit context is not live acceptance, route or travel time.

Two DCMR/RIVM air stations inside Ridderkerk reported point readings at 2026-09-02T17:00Z. No KNMI or Waterinfo station lies inside; nearest weather is Rotterdam Airport about 14.755 km away and nearest water observation is Krimpen aan de Lek about 3.425 km away. These are parameter/time-specific observations, not municipal fields or a synthetic T+72 forecast.

No in-boundary 365-day seismic event and no assigned local NDW situation are scoped cache no-matches. Each register/observation retains publisher, version, location/coverage, observed/issued/retrieved time, quality/licence and affectsSimulation=false; no-match never means normal, open, connected or safe.

findings.action: Retain zero only for the narrow direct open-coast distance contribution. Suppress any all-water/coastal-safety interpretation and implement selected tidal/storm-surge/river/barrier scenarios with explicit source and control state; never add independent proximity fields as physical depth.

residualLimitations: This audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a forecast, warning, flood assessment, evacuation plan, industrial-plume model, public-health instruction or operator commitment.
CBS values are rounded/suppressed and neighbourhood totals need not equal the municipality total; null district-heating/charging and absent operational records remain Unknown.

The overview boundary is selection/aggregation geometry only; full-resolution and native dike, outside-dike, hydraulic, sewer, groundwater, road, industrial and asset geometry is required for intersection.
Municipal stress maps, historic rainfall and project documents support mechanism eligibility/planning, not validation of the generic 2.824965762 m model value or a current event.
Benedenrivieren water levels couple river discharge, sea level/tide, wind and barrier operation; open-coast and river proximity screens cannot be interpreted independently as physical hydraulics.
Municipal/HWH/WSHD assets do not establish connected catchments, compatible throughput, live controls, power/backup, receiving levels, overflow, quality or restoration.

Riverfront/environmental and regional-risk records identify industrial/hazmat eligibility, not current inventory, release, plume, exposed population, firefighting resources, compliance or environmental effect.

NWB/NDW/ProRail/GTFS and operator project pages do not establish incident-time road, junction, bridge, tunnel, rail/transit state, vehicles, emergency exemptions, evacuation capacity or care reachability.
The 4–7, 9–10 and 11–14 September and 2–5 October road-work windows were future on the 3 September audit reference; publication or schedule existence is not a present restriction.

No complete public physical electricity, gas, drinking-water, wastewater, telecom, facility, fuel, stock, staff, backup, repair or restoration topology is consumed; sensitive gaps remain Unknown or synthetic.
Resident allocation omits workers, school/care occupants, visitors, evacuees, responders and road/waterway/transit transients at event time.
Air, weather and water observations are point/time samples; no local station or no assigned event/restriction never establishes a municipality-wide condition.
Direct wildfire zero is only a narrow no-selected-ignition model result; urban/industrial fire and regional smoke are separate pathways. No recent in-boundary seismic event is not a future guarantee.
Earthquake, cyber, heat, winter and severe-storm presets remain generic exercises unless a named event/target and valid-time forcing are selected.
The 72-hour horizon excludes prolonged displacement, contamination, health effects, economic/process losses, environmental remediation, reconstruction and adaptive behaviour.
